extracted.intended_audience: Current NACTEP grantees, potential NACTEP applicants, tribal colleges and organizations, program administrators, and Department of Education staff
extracted.subtask_description: Federal Register notice announcing final waivers of specific Department of Education regulations to extend the project period for FY2007 Native American Career and Technical Education Program (NACTEP) grants by 12 months, and explaining criteria and procedures for continuation awards and related regulatory analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of 34 CFR 75.250 and 75.261(c)(2) (project-period limitations)
rubrics_metrics.description: For 60-month projects funded in FY 2007 under NACTEP, the Secretary waives 34 CFR 75.250 and 75.261(c)(2) in order to extend the project period of these current NACTEP grants for an additional 12 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This waiver allows the 30 current NACTEP grantees to seek FY 2012 continuation awards for their current projects through FY 2013 and means the Department will not announce a new NACTEP competition in FY 2012.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation award decision criteria (information to be considered)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department will make decisions regarding continuation awards based on information provided in NACTEP grantee requests for continuation awards, including information provided in program narratives, budgets and budget narratives, and performance reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantees should supply complete program narratives, detailed budgets and budget narratives, and up-to-date performance reports to support continuation requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that continuation awards demonstrate substantial progress (34 CFR 75.253)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any requests for continuation awards will be subject to the requirements of 34 CFR 75.253, including the requirement that each grantee demonstrate that it is making substantial progress performing its NACTEP grant activities based on the requirements in the March 2007 notice inviting applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrating 'substantial progress' means showing continued implementation consistent with grant requirements and the March 2007 approved application; grantees must document accomplishments and ongoing activities as described under 34 CFR 75.253.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency/logical extension of approved scope, goals, and objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Any activities to be carried out during the continuation year must be consistent with, or be a logical extension of the scope, goals, and objectives of each grantee's application as approved in the 2007 NACTEP competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuation activities should not depart from the approved project purpose; they may reasonably extend or build on previously approved work streams, partnerships, participant cohorts, and program plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: March 2007 notice continues to govern current projects
rubrics_metrics.description: The March 2007 notice will continue to govern current projects during the extension year and the 30 applications approved under the March 2007 notice will govern continuation activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The March 2007 notice established a project period of up to 60 months, explained program requirements, described evaluation and reporting requirements, and established GPRA performance indicators for NACTEP; grantees should follow those terms during the extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of delayed effective date / good-cause justification
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary determined that a delayed effective date is unnecessary and contrary to the public interest and invoked the good-cause exception to the Administrative Procedure Act's delayed effective date requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The determination cites (1) strong public comment support (81 of 82 comments), (2) only minor editorial changes between proposed and final notices, (3) the short (12-month) additional funding period, and (4) the need to make timely continuation grants to affected entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act certification (economic impact on small entities)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary certifies that the waivers and extension and the activities required to support an additional year of NACTEP funding will not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale given: only the 30 currently-funded NACTEP grantees (small entities) are affected; waivers impose minimal compliance costs because they extend existing projects; activities can be funded from program funds and do not impose additional regulatory burdens or unnecessary Federal supervision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act statement
rubrics_metrics.description: This notice of waivers and extension does not contain any information collection requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No new PRA approvals or burden estimates are required for this notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intergovernmental Review applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: The NACTEP is not subject to Executive Order 12372 and the regulations in 34 CFR part 79.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State single-point-of-contact review under EO 12372 does not apply to this program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility of document in alternative formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals with disabilities can obtain this document in an accessible format (e.g., braille, large print, audiotape, or compact disc) on request to either of the contact persons listed under FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantees and the public may request accessible formats from the named contacts (Gwen Washington; Linda Mayo) and use FRS/TDD/TTY contact procedures if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy decision: no new NACTEP competition in FY2012
rubrics_metrics.description: As a result of the waiver and extension, the Department will not announce a new NACTEP competition in FY 2012.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a future competition is held (e.g., FY 2013 or later), the Department will announce it via Federal Register notice inviting applications and will include information such as grant period length.
